title: Latency budget & fallback notes (scratchpad)
content:
Notes to self — latency budget and fallback protocol scratchpad

Context and goal
- Trying to land a safer, deterministic canary flow for model swaps (v1 -> v1.1) that prioritizes latency SLOs across regions and reduces noisy rollbacks.
- Focus: define concrete latency budgets (token and response), automated gates, fallback model mapping, and quick rollback/runbook snippets for SREs and on-call.

Assumptions
- Hosted API and Dedicated share same routing policies; private deployments may not have automated fallback.
- We have telemetry for p50/p90/p95/p99 response times per model+route and per-customer API key.
- KV prefix caching reduces tail latency for repeat requests — but cache warming is uneven across regions.

Quick TL;DR policy idea
1) Canary traffic window: 0.5% -> 3% -> 10% -> 30% over N minutes with hold times tied to metrics (not just time).
2) Latency gating: block progress if p95_latency increases > 15% vs baseline OR p99 absolute crosses threshold.
3) Error gating: block on 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase or user-facing error-rate (> user_err_code) > 0.2%.
4) Auto-fallback: on gate trip, route affected cohorts to fallback variant (quantized / smaller model) and mark canary as paused.

Concrete latency budgets (starting point) — per-route baseline dependent
- latency_budget_p50: baseline_p50 * 1.10 (allow 10% headroom)
- latency_budget_p95: max(baseline_p95 * 1.15, baseline_p95 + 30ms)
- latency_budget_p99: baseline_p99 + 80ms hard cap
- token-generation budget: prefer per-token ms budget for streaming paths (baseline_token_ms * 1.25)

Examples (numbers for text-generation routes)
- baseline p95 = 380ms -> budget = max(380*1.15=437ms, +30ms -> 410ms) => pick 437ms
- baseline p99 = 820ms -> budget = 900ms cap (since +80ms = 900ms)

Telemetry queries to run before/after each step (placeholder examples)
- Summaries: SELECT percentile(response_ms, 50,95,99) FROM traces WHERE model = "$MODEL" AND route = "$ROUTE" AND window = last(30m) GROUP BY region
- Error spikes: count(status >= 500) / total_requests over rolling 15m
- Client-impacting: logs with user_error_meta != null -> ratio over 60m

Gate evaluation logic (pseudo)
- For each hold-window W: compute new_percentiles and compare to baseline_buckets (same day-of-week, same hour if possible).
- If any region exceeds gated thresholds -> escalate: pause rollout and launch fallback mapping for affected region/cohort.
- If only a non-production test key or synthetic traffic shows regression -> annotate and continue hold if human approves.

Fallback mappings (practical plan)
- Primary -> Fallback candidates: v1.1.full_fp16 -> v1.1.q8_0 (quantized) -> v1.stable (previous production)
- Route-level fallback: for long-tail clients with known low-throughput patterns, route to cached-output layer if available.
- Pin mapping example: {"client_cohort": "beta-users", "on_fallback": "v1.stable", "reason": "p95 regression"} (store as simple k/v in rollout metadata)

Runbook snippets (commands & quick actions)
- Pause rollout: POST /api/rollouts/{id}/pause  (CLI: rwdctl rollout pause {id})
- Set fallback: POST /api/rollouts/{id}/set-fallback {"cohort":"X","model":"v1.stable"}
- Rollback immediately to previous: rwdctl release rollback --release-id {release} --to-version v1.stable --force
- Emergency circuit-breaker: rwdctl cluster scale-down --route {route} --replicas 0. (only for extreme cases after paging SRE)

Observability checklist during canary hold
- Live dashboards: per-route p95, p99, throughput, qps, 5xx rate, user_err_rate, avg token_ms
- Synthetic probe set: run 5 warmup probes + 50 traffic profile tests that mirror top 10 customer prompts
- KV cache hit rate by region — low hit-rate might explain tail regressions after model change
- Cost signal: tokens/sec and GPU utilization to catch runaway side-effects (memory thrash -> tails)

Open questions / TODOs
- How long should we keep the fallback pinned for a paused canary? (24h vs until manual clear?)
- Should rollback be automated after X minutes of paused state with no human ack? (risk: flip-flopping)
- We need a small UI affordance in Console to show "active fallback" per-route/cohort — file a design ticket.
- Add a small synthetic suite to product-tests repo that focuses on cold-cache tails (RDW-2425).

Experiment ideas
- Reduce initial canary to 0.1% for high-risk models (large sequence / long-context) and use longer hold windows but more strict telemetry (p99 focus).
- Gradual warm-up for KV cache: route warmup traffic to canary nodes for first 30m to populate prefix caches before counting latency windows.
- Shadow traffic: send 100% shadow to v1.1 without impacting production path, measure differences and produce a delta dashboard (low-risk evaluation).

Human notes / reminders
- Tell Marco and Eva before next run — they want the p99 heatmap updated.
- Mention this draft in next eng sync and get buy-in for gating thresholds.
- Leave a snippet in the runbook for on-call: top 3 diagnostics to run in first 10 minutes.

Quick on-call diagnostics (10-minute checklist)
1) Check per-region p95/p99 and 5xxs, compare to 1h baseline.
2) Confirm KV cache hit-rate and memory pressure on GPU nodes.
3) If p99 spikes but errors are flat, consider increasing replicas briefly or pin fallback; if errors spike, rollback.

Linked references (todo convert to proper Confluence)
- CONFLUENCE: Latency Budgeting playbook (draft) — /display/RDW/Latency+Budgeting
- JIRA: RDW-2319 (rollout gating infra), RDW-2425 (synthetic cold-cache tests)
- GH PR: runtime/pull/789 (routing policy changes)

End of scratchpad. Keep iterating.
